251.s: The band rehearsed nearly every day, with no lateness or grumbling.
251.q: We were traveling. We would get into a town early and maybe rest a little while and I would call a rehearsal. And then, of course, the guys would tell me, say, old man, call a rehearsal. We got a new arrangement to be back together. Well, no problem. Nobody late. Nobody grouchy.

251.t: Band billing names and rehearsing on the road
251.s: From Don Albert and his Ten Pals to America's Greatest Swing Band; rehearsals were fitted into layoffs.
251.q: Every time we could get a chance. You know, being a traveling band on the road and you stay up all night, you have to pick the times. And the times you were playing, maybe you had a couple of dates or you had a couple of days lay off. Well, I would call it a rehearsal and we'd rehearse that way.…

174.t: Reading music and rehearsals in the Holy Ghost band
174.s: Old bands used sheet music and rehearsed twice a week; Dejan was kept in the band because he could read. Some current bands play tunes like Panama Rag the short way.
174.q: Yes, they did. They did. Because you see, and before, when you're playing the brass band, you have to rehearse them. See when I was playing the Holy Ghost brass band, my dad had a voice about my youth plant clarinet. I was a youngster, in my teens. But we had to rehearse them at the Holy Ghost Hall…

776.t: Rehearsing the band: a perfectionist coach and tuning
776.s: Verne explains how the bands rehearsed regularly and a vocal coach taught them to tune.
776.ch: Bandleaders and talent on the boats
776.q: No. No. No. The white artists have always just been used to do since I brought to all the talent. They never did. In the old days, we were much more interested in the band. But now we're just going seven nights a week. It was very important that we had a good band. The band rehearsed regularly.…

58.t: Rehearsing by head: Buddy and Zeb, George Boyd, Eddie Marsh
58.s: Punch says bands rarely rehearsed, praises the Petit-Zeb pairing and names his clarinetist George Boyd and Eddie Marsh.
58.q: Well, yeah. That's why I say a few of the things like, he know the song and I learned it and something in there he wanted me to catch. Well, he tell me, you know. How I'd go and everything, I learned on the horns. Play it in there.

833.s: He recalls a band rehearsing in a church hall near Charity Hospital where others stood behind him as he read.
833.ch: Clarinet and lessons with Jim Humphrey
833.q: Exactly, that's the place. I know the other one. Well, we used to go there and everybody, everybody stand in the back of me, you know, see if I'm reading this right, you know. And they said, it's doggone, I used to play at them partners, you know. I was in the band with them there, a pretty…

520.s: Silver rehearsed thoroughly while Cannonball's band was more spontaneous.
520.q: Yes, we rehearsed, but it wasn’t like Horace though. Now Horace rehearsed quite a bit. And when he went into the studio Horace — we had played the choruses, played the compositions, so all the little things were worked out, what we were going to do. But with Cannon it wasn’t like that. 336.t: Big band drumming and the Monday night band at Pearl's
336.s: Big band skills came from casuals; he now plays the Monday Night Big Band with Thad Jones and Oliver Nelson charts.
336.q: Yeah. I mean actually I did it, I mean that was part of my experience and training coming up, and a lot of the gigs we did, casuals or club dates, had to do with big bands, so that was a skill that was valuable. And I sort of spent some time at it. And then I didn’t do it for a long time, there…

522.t: Organizing the big band and adding to the book
522.s: The big band never rehearses; he gathered the best players regionally, and new songs come from requests.
522.ch: Style, repertoire and the music business
522.q: Oh for one thing. The big band was predicated — there was a date here in Rochester that turned into two dozen dates the first year, on Monday nights, at a dance club, and when I say dance club, I mean that kind of dance club. And I decided that I would put the best musicians that I could possibly…

346.t: Leading groups and rehearsing every day
346.s: Asked how he guided groups, he says they rehearsed nine to five every day because taking music for granted means losing.
346.ch: Performing and the idea of free jazz
346.q: Well you know we rehearsed man. You know. We rehearsed every day you know. I mean like you wouldn’t have to ask me what are you doing Monday through Friday — you know — we’re rehearsing you know. From about nine to five every day. That’s what we’re doing. You know. I mean like you can’t, you know…

367.t: What a battle of the bands was; Gerald as a rehearsal leader
367.s: Snooky explains the hour-long sets of a battle and praises Gerald's first band and his skill at rehearsing.
367.q: No, you played a set. You played about an hour. A four-hour engagement we would play hour — hour — hour — hour. That’s the way it would be. But the people, you know, was there to see who was going to blow who out. That was the whole idea.

469.t: His rehearsal band at the union
469.s: The no-pressure rehearsal band he led with top players.
469.q: Boy that’s a good question man. Well actually I had a rehearsal band with some good arrangements and that was fun. I would call a rehearsal, I’d call up the guys, great players, everybody would always say yes I’ll be there, for no money, for two hours maybe in between shows. And we’d play whatever…

110.t: Rehearsing and preparation in the quartet's early years
110.s: Most development happened on the job, with rehearsals mainly for new recorded material such as Eurasia.
110.ch: Fantasy Records, the accident and the quartet
110.q: Occasionally there would be rehearsals in preparation for a recording, if it was new material that you had not played in concert or in clubs. The [Jazz Impressions of] Eurasia album, I think there were a few rehearsals, because it was all new.

165.s: Rehearsals are long debates; they repeat tunes until he says they are right, because audiences know these songs.
165.q: Yeah. That’s true. That’s true. I like it to be right, because then people will hear it. Because people already know these tunes that we do. They’re part of America’s culture, and I think if you do them wrong, people know. They may not be musicians. They may not have any real sophistication and be…

505.t: How he became a big-band leader
505.s: Through school clinics, student arrangers wrote charts of his tunes, and he fronts the band on soprano.
505.ch: Later bands and the Saxophone Summit
505.q: From the schools, because when you’re invited to do a weekend and a clinic, you’re going to end up playing with the high school – the college band. Guys would write charts for me. They said, “Can I take your tunes?” “ Be my guest. I would never – I have no idea about big-band writing. I think…

230.t: Southland Cafe in Boston after the fire
230.s: After the one-nighter trip they rehearsed new charts at the Southland Cafe in Boston.
230.ch: The Famous Door, Billy May and the Palomar fire
230.q: To the Southland. Well, one nighted across the country, to the Southland Cafe in Boston, and then we did a lot of rehearsing and put all the new charts in, and got back to a more disciplined way of playing, because we were romping pretty good on that trip, as you can imagine, you know, with mostly…

67.s: DeParis's routines never changed but he kept the band on its toes, which Cheatham liked.

70.t: Section rehearsals and Redman's rule to follow the first man
70.s: Calloway was not a technical musician, so the sidemen rehearsed sections themselves; Jackson recalls Redman's advice to phrase with the lead player.
70.q: too, that a lot of times if a guy made an arrangement, whoever made the arrangement, sometime Calloway would have him just run it over.

92.s: Between jobs he rehearsed with Redman's band, where musicians played hearts and rehearsals started hours late.

72.t: Joining Wilbur De Paris: rehearsals and Atlantic records
72.s: De Paris rehearsed twice a week for two months at Ryan's before the 1952 Atlantic recordings.
72.ch: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris

124.t: Using idle weeks in the theater to rehearse
124.s: During five weeks in the theater McRae and Jeff rehearsed the book and the other sections joined.
124.ch: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
124.q: Because you remember when we was in the theater, oh about -- we was in the theater about five weeks. We wasn't doing nothing.

13.t: Discipline and rehearsals in the Hines band
13.ch: Breakup of Hines band to Lefty Bates
13.q: We'd have a whole bunch of music. Now at the show -- rehearse with a piano player until the day before the show was to go in. Maybe might rehearse two days before the show. Then we'd have a dress rehearsal the same morning, when we'd get off, if the show was to open that night.
